name: Cast Swap
summary: Swap anyone in a video for yourself or any character: it scans the clip, maps your images to the people you pick, and writes one timestamped video-to-video prompt that keeps every move, cut and second.
use_when: The user wants to put themselves or a character into a movie scene, music video or TikTok, swap or recast an actor or singer, replace a person in a video with a reference image, restyle a clip while swapping its cast (anime, 3D animated, a show's own style), or fix a character swap that came out wrong.
produces: A scan of the uploaded clip (exact duration, cuts, every person, a timestamped timeline), then one copy-ready video-to-video prompt that states the duration, maps each reference image to the person it replaces, carries whole-second timestamps from the real cuts, and comes with attach, settings, @-tag and tool-fit notes. Long clips are split into parts that add up exactly.

name: Frame Match Character
summary: Upload a frame and your reference character, get copy-ready JSON text-to-image prompts that recreate the same shot, pose, style and composition with your character swapped in.
use_when: The user wants to recreate a screenshot, movie still or viral frame with their own character, swap the subject of an image while keeping the camera, pose and lighting, or turn a stylized frame (anime, claymation, cartoon, 3D) into a matching or photorealistic prompt.
produces: Separate copy-ready JSON prompt blocks with full frame analysis: close match + creative variant for photoreal frames, or original-style close match, original-style variant and a photorealistic adaptation for stylized frames. Text and logos removed, character locked across frames.

name: Mini Kittens
summary: Writes copy-ready prompts for viral photorealistic mini-kitten reels — palm-sized kittens standing upright in real human places, shot like candid night footage.
use_when: The user wants a kitten video or image prompt, wants a cat character sheet or a mini version of their own cat, wants kitten scene ideas or a storyboard, wants a timestamped video prompt from a storyboard, a single image or a character sheet, or wants to appear in the video with the kittens themselves.
produces: A character sheet that locks a reusable kitten cast, a storyboard of linked image prompts, or a timestamped video prompt with the length and shot count the user picks — each copy-ready, and optionally with the user written into the scene from a photo of themselves.

name: PS2 Style

use_when: You want a PS2 or GTA San Andreas style image or video; a retro low-poly game look; to turn yourself into a PS2 game character from a photo; the viral "how [city, game, film] must feel like" reel; your clothing brand or product in a PS2 game promo; empty PS2 game environments; or the next shot after an image you already made.
produces: Copy-ready image prompts (single shot, panel shot or continue from your image), each with its matching timestamped video prompt in the same reply; 5 to 15 second Free Style videos; the 8-shot Nostalgia reel with an edit plan and cut points; promo shots built around your product photo; a four-view character sheet; connected empty environments; idea menus of 10 and five next-shot ideas under every shot; model, attach and settings lines for GPT Image 2 and Wan 3.0; optional generation through the OpenArt or Higgsfield MCP.

summary: Cinematic prompt studio for the Wan video model: film-grade character sheets, shot-by-shot storyboards, timed Wan video prompts with or without dialogue, and five matching environments for one world, in your character's own style or one of ten styles.
use_when: The user wants a character sheet or turnaround from an idea or a reference image, a storyboard for a video idea, or a timed Wan or Wan 3.0 video prompt with or without dialogue; or backgrounds, environments, locations or sets for a character or a story: with or without a character image, matched to the character's look or in a style they pick (photoreal, anime, 2D cartoon, 3D animated, claymation, pixel art and more). Also when they want themselves in a Wan video built from scratch, from their own photo.
produces: Copy-ready prompts, each in its own code block: a film-grade character sheet; a shot-by-shot storyboard with the shot count and length the user picks; a timed Wan 3.0 video prompt with or without dialogue, under 2,000 characters (3,000 for 20-30 seconds), with a Wan settings line; or five standalone JSON background prompts for one world (1 main location and 4 connected places, each with camera angle, framing, lens, lighting and a negative prompt), empty so characters can be placed in later. Every answer ends with a next step, so a character, its world, its storyboard and its video connect.
